tools.name: redactwell
tools.description: Black out text in a PDF permanently, in your browser — the covered words are physically removed, not just hidden. Drag black boxes or use Find & redact to place a box over every match of a word; redacted pages are rasterised and flattened to images so the text layer under each bar is destroyed, untouched pages are copied verbatim, and document metadata is dropped. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: pdf.js (pdfjs-dist) + its Web Worker — parse + render each page to a canvas, and extract the text layer (getTextContent + Util.transform) for Find & redact
Canvas 2D — rasterise each redacted page at the chosen DPI and paint the black bars into the pixels (padded to over-cover), so redaction is burned in rather than layered on top
pdf-lib in a dedicated Web Worker — rebuild the output PDF: embed flattened page images, copyPages untouched pages verbatim, and strip document metadata (author/title/producer)
First-party redaction geometry — normalized 0..1 boxes (orientation-agnostic), drag→box, pad/over-cover, page→pixel mapping, flatten-plan, DPI→scale (all unit-tested)
Pointer Events — draw / move / delete redaction rectangles, with a draw-vs-scroll mode toggle (touch-action none only in draw mode) so drawing and scrolling don't fight on a phone
IntersectionObserver — lazily render page canvases as they scroll into view
Transferable ArrayBuffer — zero-copy of the source bytes + rasterised page images to the assembly worker
requestAnimationFrame shim (native when visible, setTimeout when document.hidden) so an export keeps rendering when the tab is backgrounded — pdf.js schedules render continuations on rAF
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the PDF, anchor-download fallback)
Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard-free download path
localStorage (export DPI / sharpness / flatten-all only; never the document)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + pdf.js worker + sample precached, full offline)

tools.name: tunewell
tools.description: A chromatic instrument tuner in your browser — tune guitar, bass, ukulele or violin by microphone or by ear, with a downloadable reference-tone pitch pipe (WAV). Live cents dial with per-string in-tune lights, first-party McLeod (MPM) pitch detection, selectable reference A (415–444 Hz), and a pitch-over-time report from an uploaded recording. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: getUserMedia (live microphone — the sensor input; echo-cancellation/noise-suppression/AGC off so the detector sees the true waveform; never connected to destination, so no earpiece-routing/feedback; tracks stopped on teardown/pagehide)

First-party pitch detection — McLeod's Pitch Method (MPM): NSDF with the autocorrelation term via a hand-written radix-2 FFT, running sum-of-squares normalisation, key-maxima picking (octave-error resistant) and parabolic sub-sample interpolation. No runtime library.
First-party note maths (frequency↔MIDI↔cents, selectable reference A 415–444 Hz, sharp/flat naming) and per-string nearest-match by cents distance
Web Audio AnalyserNode (getFloatTimeDomainData tap on the live stream)
Web Audio OscillatorNode + GainNode (live reference-tone playback — the pitch pipe)
First-party 16-bit PCM WAV encoder + reference-tone synthesiser (fundamental + harmonics, raised-cosine fades) — renders the downloadable pitch-pipe WAV artefact
Web Workers (frame-by-frame pitch trace of a whole uploaded recording off the main thread)
Transferable ArrayBuffer (decoded PCM to the worker)
Canvas 2D (live −50…+50 cents dial with in-tune band + needle; 1200×675 pitch-over-time report card)
setInterval tuner loop at ~20 Hz (a hidden tab throttles rAF to a halt)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the WAV/PNG/CSV, with anchor-download fallback)
Clipboard API (summary text + ClipboardItem report image)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + sample precached)

tools.name: wavewell
tools.description: Turn a podcast clip, voice memo or song into a shareable waveform video (audiogram) in your browser — animated dancing-spectrum, mirror or sweeping-waveform styles, a caption, an optional background image, and portrait/square/landscape output for social. Rendered to an H.264 + AAC MP4 entirely on-device with WebCodecs; nothing is uploaded, no watermark, works offline.
browser_apis: WebCodecs (H.264 video encode from canvas frames, via mediabunny CanvasSource; getFirstEncodableVideoCodec('avc') capability gate with a Chrome/Edge/Safari notice)
mediabunny (Output + Mp4OutputFormat + BufferTarget — the fleet's first tool that GENERATES video rather than transcoding it; no COOP/COEP needed)
mediabunny AudioSampleSource (planar f32 AudioSample chunks re-encoded to AAC uniformly across input formats) + @mediabunny/aac-encoder (WASM fallback registered in-worker)

Web Audio API (AudioContext.decodeAudioData for any input format; AudioBufferSourceNode for the live preview — worker can't construct an AudioContext, so decode is main-thread and channel-data copies are transferred)
OffscreenCanvas + Canvas 2D (per-frame render shared between the worker encode and the main-thread preview)
Web Workers (whole render→encode pipeline off the main thread; postMessage progress, no rAF to avoid the hidden-tab hang)

First-party DSP: radix-2 Cooley–Tukey FFT + Hann window, log-spaced spectrum banding (40 Hz–16 kHz) with dB mapping, whole-clip peak-envelope extraction, fast-attack/slow-release temporal smoothing — no runtime DSP library
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the MP4, with anchor-download fallback)
Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard API (ClipboardItem video)
localStorage (style/aspect/palette/sensitivity settings only; never the caption or audio)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + sample precached, AAC-encoder JS served)

tools.name: ditherwell
tools.description: Turn any photo into retro dithered pixel-art in your browser — 1-bit black & white, Game Boy, CGA, grayscale/sepia, or an adaptive palette drawn from the image. Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson, Jarvis, Stucki and ordered Bayer dithering, live before/after, exported as a crisp blocky PNG. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: Web Workers (whole decode→dither→encode pipeline off the main thread; job-id multiplexing so a newer render supersedes an in-flight one)
createImageBitmap + OffscreenCanvas (worker-side decode, smooth downsample by pixel-size, and nearest-neighbour upscale for crisp blocky output)

First-party dithering DSP — error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson, Jarvis–Judice–Ninke, Stucki) with serpentine scanning, plus ordered 4×4/8×8 Bayer dithering with a palette-adaptive perturbation amplitude — no runtime library
First-party median-cut adaptive palette (2–32 colours from the image) + fixed palettes (1-bit, Game Boy DMG, CGA, grayscale, sepia ramps) + squared-Euclidean nearest-colour
First-party brightness/contrast pre-adjustment in the pixel domain
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the PNG, with anchor-download fallback)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + sample precached, offline)

tools.name: noisewell
tools.description: A sound level meter in your browser — measure noise in decibels with your microphone, log it over time, and export a report (Leq, Lmax, L10/L90 as a chart and CSV). A live dB(A) readout with hearing-safety colour coding, octave spectrum, and a first-class upload-a-file path. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: getUserMedia (live microphone — the sensor input; echo-cancellation/noise-suppression/AGC off so the meter reads the true level; tracks stopped + context closed on teardown/hide/unload)
Web Audio AnalyserNode (getFloatTimeDomainData tap on the live stream; never connected to destination, so no earpiece-routing/feedback problem)
OfflineAudioContext (decodeAudioData for the uploaded-file / mic-denied fallback path)

First-party DSP: radix-2 FFT + Hann window, IEC 61672 A/C-weighting curves applied as a spectral correction to the broadband RMS, Fast/Slow exponential ballistics in the power domain, 1/1-octave banding — no runtime library
First-party acoustics statistics: Leq (energy average), Lmax/Lmin, L10/L50/L90 exceedance percentiles, sample-peak
Web Workers (frame-by-frame FFT of a whole uploaded recording off the main thread)
Transferable ArrayBuffer (decoded PCM to the worker)
Canvas 2D (live level bar with safety zones + peak-hold, scrolling history, octave spectrum, and the 1200×675 report card)
setInterval meter loop (a hidden tab throttles rAF to a halt)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the report PNG/CSV, with anchor-download fallback)
Clipboard API (summary text + ClipboardItem report image)
localStorage (weighting / time constant / calibration offset only)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + sample precached)

tools.name: vectorwell
tools.description: Turn a PNG, JPG or photo into a clean, scalable SVG in your browser — colour (posterised) or black & white line-art tracing with Potrace compiled to WebAssembly, tuned live with a before/after slider. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: esm-potrace-wasm (Potrace raster→vector tracing, WASM — colour posterised + black & white; wasm inlined into the worker bundle, served same-origin, offline)
Web Workers (decode + down-scale + trace off the main thread; job-id multiplexing so a newer trace supersedes an in-flight one)
createImageBitmap + OffscreenCanvas (worker-side decode and pre-scale to the chosen trace resolution)
Canvas 2D (source + SVG render for the compare slider; PNG rasterisation of the SVG for clipboard)
Pointer Events + clip-path (before/after raster-vs-vector compare slider)
First-party SVG tidy (viewBox/namespace normalise, coordinate rounding + DTD strip without touching fill colours)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker, with anchor-download fallback)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + worker/wasm precached)

tools.name: embiggen
tools.description: Upscale and enhance small or low-resolution images in your browser with a Swin2SR super-resolution model — 2× or 4×, on WebGPU with a WASM fallback. Nothing is uploaded; the image never leaves the tab, and it works offline after the model downloads once.
browser_apis: @huggingface/transformers (Swin2SR image-to-image super-resolution; classical-x2 + realworld-x4 models, lazy-loaded per scale)
WebGPU (GPU inference) with automatic WASM/ONNX Runtime fallback
WebAssembly (ONNX Runtime Web, bundled same-origin — no CDN)
Web Workers + comlink (model + inference off the main thread)
First-party output-bound planning (pre-scale oversized inputs to keep the result ≤ 4096 px; Swin2SR has no tiling)
OffscreenCanvas + ImageData (decode via RawImage.fromBlob, encode PNG)
Pointer Events + clip-path (before/after compare slider, pointer + keyboard)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker, with anchor-download fallback)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell precached, ORT wasm served not precached)

tools.name: swatchwell
tools.description: Pick colours from your camera or any image, build a palette, and export it as CSS, JSON, PNG, SVG, ASE or GPL. Real-world eyedropping via the rear camera, median-cut extraction from images, and the screen EyeDropper — with perceptual (CIEDE2000) nearest-name matching. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: getUserMedia (rear camera — the live sensor input; torch constraint; tracks stopped on teardown/hide/unload)
EyeDropper API (screen-pixel sampling on desktop, feature-detected)
Canvas 2D / OffscreenCanvas + getImageData (reticle region sampling + PNG swatch-sheet render)
Web Workers + Transferable ArrayBuffer (first-party median-cut extraction, zero-copy)
First-party colour science (sRGB→linear→XYZ→Lab, CIEDE2000, HSL) — no runtime colour library
First-party Adobe Swatch Exchange (.ase) binary writer via DataView
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker, with anchor-download fallback)

tools.name: shakewell
tools.description: Measure vibration frequency with your phone — turn the accelerometer into a live seismograph, spectrum analyser and RPM meter. Diagnose a wobbly washing machine, fan or motor; leave with a frequency, a spectrum PNG and a CSV. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() (iOS 13+, requested inside a tap, feature-detected)
First-party radix-2 Cooley–Tukey FFT + Hann window + linear resampler (no runtime library)
Per-axis detrend + summed power spectra (avoids the |a| frequency-doubling artefact)
Parabolic sub-bin peak interpolation + integer-harmonic detection
Web Workers (large-CSV parse + full-recording FFT off the main thread)
Canvas 2D (live seismograph, live spectrum, off-screen 1200×675 PNG card)
setInterval render loop (a hidden tab throttles rAF to a halt)
File API + Blob + URL.createObjectURL (CSV in, CSV + PNG out)

tools.name: voxwell
tools.description: Change your voice in your browser — pitch and formants moved independently by a hand-written phase vocoder, live from the microphone or from a file, exported as WAV or MP3. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: AudioWorklet (first-party phase vocoder: 1024-pt Hann STFT at 4× overlap, per-bin true-frequency estimation, spectral-envelope formant warp — no library)
AudioWorklet (second processor capturing raw Float32 PCM)
First-party radix-2 FFT (the worklet must be a single import-free ES module)
getUserMedia (mono, echoCancellation/noiseSuppression/AGC off; permission requested inside a tap)
OfflineAudioContext (file rendered through the identical graph, latency-trimmed)
GainNode with audio-rate gain (true ring modulation, not tremolo)
AnalyserNode + Canvas 2D (scope + level meter, setInterval-driven so a hidden tab can't stall it)

tools.name: meshprep
tools.description: Check a 3D model before you print it — size, volume, holes and non-manifold edges drawn in red on the model itself. Converts STL/OBJ/PLY/3MF. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: WebGL2 (first-party renderer, no three.js — flat shading from fragment-shader derivatives, no normal buffer; two-sided lighting so inverted-normal meshes stay visible)
Web Workers (parse → analyse → export off the main thread)
First-party format parsers (STL binary/ASCII, OBJ, PLY ASCII/binary both endiannesses, 3MF — a worker has no DOMParser)

tools.name: reactwell
tools.description: Drop a JSX or TSX file and see the React component render instantly — transpiled in your browser with esbuild (WASM) and mounted in a sandboxed iframe. React is bundled locally; nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: esbuild-wasm (in-browser JSX/TSX transpile + bundle, worker:false inside our worker)
Import maps + data: URL ES modules (resolve bare specifiers inside the sandbox)
Sandboxed <iframe srcdoc> (allow-scripts only, opaque origin; error boundary)
React 18 UMD (vendored same-origin, no CDN — preview runtime works offline)
postMessage (runtime/compile errors streamed from the frame)
File System Access API (showOpenFilePicker + poll-to-live-watch a file)
Clipboard API + Web Share API (share-by-URL snippet)
Service Worker (PWA; app shell precached, wasm runtime-cached)

tools.name: glyphcut
tools.description: Subset fonts and convert them to WOFF2 in your browser with HarfBuzz compiled to WebAssembly — keep only the characters your site uses. Licensed font files are never uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: WebAssembly (HarfBuzz hb-subset — harfbuzz-subset.wasm vendored same-origin, hand-written raw bindings)
Web Workers (whole font pipeline; fonts held worker-side for the session)
CSS Font Loading API (FontFace — live specimen rendered from the subsetted output)

tools.name: gridwell
tools.description: Open, query and convert huge CSV files in your browser — millions of rows filtered and exported with a real SQL engine (DuckDB) compiled to WebAssembly. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm (DuckDB analytical SQL engine, eh build — vendored same-origin, no CDN)
WebAssembly (exception-handling build; no cross-origin isolation required)
Web Workers (DuckDB's own worker — all queries off the main thread)
File API + registerFileHandle (BROWSER_FILEREADER ranged reads — file never buffered into JS memory)
Clipboard API (copy cell / SQL, paste-to-ingest CSV)
Service Worker (PWA; network-first shell, runtime-cached WASM)

tools.name: papershot
tools.description: Turn a phone photo of a document into a flat, readable PDF scan — corners found automatically, perspective flattened, shadows removed. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: First-party computer vision (Scharr gradient, convex hull, max-area quad, 4-point homography, bilinear inverse warp, integral-image adaptive threshold) — no OpenCV
Web Workers (whole CV pipeline; raw RGBA in and out)

tools.name: blurwell
tools.description: Blur faces in photos and video in your browser — automatic on-device face detection plus manual boxes for plates and badges, with the blur burned into the exported pixels. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: @mediapipe/tasks-vision (BlazeFace FaceDetector, WASM — model + runtime vendored same-origin)

tools.name: vidwell
tools.description: Compress and trim video in your browser — shrink a big MP4/MOV, cap the resolution, cut a clip, export a smaller MP4. Decode → H.264 encode happens on-device via WebCodecs; nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: verisum
tools.description: Compute and verify file checksums (SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5, BLAKE3…) in your browser — stream a file through a WASM hasher and match it against a published checksum. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: provenova
tools.description: The vendor-neutral system of record for quantum computing — capture, reproduce, benchmark, and attest quantum runs across any QPU or vendor.

tools.name: screenwell
tools.description: Record your screen — with mic, system audio and an optional webcam bubble — entirely in your browser. MediaRecorder encodes locally; nothing is uploaded. Works offline.

tools.name: pixpress
tools.description: Compress and convert images to WebP, JPEG, AVIF or PNG in your browser using @jsquash WASM encoders, with a before/after compare slider. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: inkwell
tools.description: Sign and fill PDFs entirely in your browser — draw/type/upload a signature, place text, dates, initials and checkmarks, download a flattened PDF. Nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: pagesmith
tools.description: Merge, split, reorder, rotate and delete PDF pages entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: unheic
tools.description: Convert iPhone HEIC & HEIF photos to JPG, PNG or WebP in your browser with libheif (WASM). No uploads; works offline.

tools.name: tokenpeek

tools.name: scribewell
tools.description: Transcribe audio & video to text and subtitles (.srt/.vtt) entirely in your browser with OpenAI Whisper. No uploads, no accounts; works offline.

tools.name: gifsmith
tools.description: Turn any video into an animated GIF entirely in your browser. No uploads, no watermark; works offline.

tools.name: zipsafe
tools.description: Create and extract ZIP archives entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: veilpix
tools.description: Hide an AES-256 encrypted message or file inside an ordinary image via LSB steganography, in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: sealbox
tools.description: Lock any file with a password in your browser using AES-256. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: metascrub
tools.description: Strip hidden metadata (GPS, camera serial, timestamps) from photos losslessly, in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: bgwipe
tools.description: Erase image backgrounds in your browser with an in-browser ML model (RMBG-1.4). Photos never leave your device.

tools.name: pdf-crush
tools.description: Compress PDFs in your browser using MozJPEG WASM. No uploads, no accounts, no server.

tools.name: dropwell
tools.description: End-to-end encrypted peer-to-peer file sharing in the browser. No backend, no installs.

tools.name: qrforge
tools.description: Generate tracking-free QR codes and scan them, entirely in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: textlift
tools.description: Extract text from images, screenshots and scanned PDFs entirely in your browser with Tesseract WASM — plain text or searchable PDF out. No uploads; English works offline.

tools.name: clipwell
